themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints exploded to 6 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 4,700% spike (z-score: 17.76)—suggesting a sudden, coordinated campaign or enforcement gap in CD 314 that emerged THIS WEEK.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 17.76 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Represents a sudden emergence rather than gradual trend
reporting_angles: Where are the illegal postings concentrated (blocks, commercial corridors)? Is there a geographic pattern?
Interview residents and business owners in hotspot areas about visibility and impact on streetscape
Investigate whether a specific campaign (political, real estate marketing, event promotion) is driving the surge

themes_detail.label: Construction Complaint Surge
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints surged to 76 last week versus a baseline of 13.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 474% spike (z-score: 13.55)—coinciding with 324 active DOB permit filings, suggesting widespread renovation activity is impacting residents.
evidence: 76 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 13.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (474% increase)
Z-score of 13.55 indicates statistically severe anomaly
324 total DOB alteration/new building permits filed in last 90 days, with 243 alteration permits concentrated in recent period
Multiple active rezonings (1455 Coney Island Ave, 2586 Nostrand Ave, 1584 Flatbush Ave) may be triggering development activity
reporting_angles: Map where the 324 DOB permits cluster geographically—are certain blocks or corridors being renovated simultaneously?
Interview residents experiencing noise, dust, or water disruptions from ongoing construction; capture daily impact
Profile how many permits are tied to the active ULURP rezonings vs. routine apartment/storefront work

themes_detail.label: Water System Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints peaked at 57 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 16.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 240% spike (z-score: 5.75)—indicating potential distribution failures, contamination concerns, or pressure issues affecting multiple households.
evidence: 57 water system complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 16.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (240% spike)
Z-score of 5.75 indicates high statistical significance
Timing overlaps with construction complaint spike (76 last week), suggesting possible pipe damage or work-related disruptions
Heat/hot water complaints remain elevated (5,507 over 90 days), potentially compounded by water system issues
reporting_angles: Obtain DEP maintenance logs for CD 314—were water mains repaired, flushed, or damaged in the past 2–3 weeks?
Interview residents about water quality (discoloration, pressure drops, temperature fluctuations) and timeline of when issues started
Investigate whether the construction spike correlates with accidental water line strikes or contractor-caused shutdowns

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality & Pigeon Spike
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints doubled (8 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 3.6 baseline, z-score: 6.29) and unsanitary pigeon conditions spiked 700% (4 vs. 0.5, z-score: 4.95) around the same period, suggesting potential pest infestation, mold, or ventilation failures concentrated in buildings.
evidence: Indoor air quality complaints at 8 (3 weeks ago) vs. 3.6 weekly baseline (121% increase, z-score: 6.29)
Unsanitary pigeon conditions at 4 complaints (3 weeks ago) vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score: 4.95)
Both spikes occurred at same time (3 weeks ago), suggesting related root cause (e.g., building disrepair, open windows attracting birds, HVAC failures)
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings generated multiple complaints—are there common factors (age, type, landlord)?
Interview residents with asthma, allergies, or respiratory issues about symptoms and whether building maintenance was deferred
Investigate whether pigeon spike is linked to reduced building maintenance (open vents, blocked screens) rather than citywide pest pressure

themes_detail.label: Parking Demand Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints dropped 52% this week (119 vs. 247.1 weekly average over 8 weeks, z-score: -4.74), a statistically significant decline that may reflect behavior change from new enforcement, permit policy shifts, or reduced street activity.
evidence: 119 illegal parking complaints THIS WEEK vs. 247.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (52% decrease)
Z-score of -4.74 indicates statistically significant change
Decline is sharp and recent, not gradual—suggests policy or enforcement shift rather than seasonal pattern
reporting_angles: Did NYPD or NYC DOT increase enforcement, towing, or ticket volume this week? Cross-reference with agency data.
Has residential or commercial activity declined (e.g., fewer commuters, holiday period), reducing parking demand?
Check whether a new permit program, parking facility opening, or commercial development change altered parking supply
